question: Can source-blind A/B archives prevent causal B-specific corruption versus the same model exposed only to continuing A, once ordinary additional A learning is controlled by an identical checkpoint fork?
role: Independent source-only Yggdrasil PR #1327 contributor, canonical integration owner Amalgam PR #1278.

source.source_rule: t0..15 common hidden H0 A; deep-cold-clone each model into paired control-A and treatment-B at t16. Control A remains H0 through t47; treatment hidden H2 B t16..31, then unannounced H0 A t32..47. Only public t,c=t%4,a=t%4,witnessed y enter any model, no fork or regime labels.
source.noise: SHA256('know31:private:coin:v1:'+mid+':'+seed+':'+t), first64/2^64, identical exogenous coin both forks, actual action-conditioned outcome differs when laws differ.
source.reward: Bernoulli .85 if TRUE_MAPS[mid][action] XOR public c produces active Boolean 1, else .15; same already frozen H0/H2 causal law evaluators.
source.fit: Reuse previously CONSUMED KNOW26 108 mapping FIT witnesses and KNOW30 128 labelled A/B FIT witnesses per map/group as historical training. Count 236 extra FIT observations/map; no new FIT or original source first-use.

arms: KNOW30 archive: same full 6x256 posterior pair with posterior-threshold quarantine, completely unchanged source
KNOW30 switching_bayes: two full 6x256 posterior slots with fractional responsibility updates, approximate HMM not exact
KNOW30 single: one continuously learned full 6x256 posterior
KNOW30 rolling8: refitted posterior from last8 public witnesses; smaller effective capacity, explicitly not primary strongest matched control

metrics.old_A_loss: Expected Brier q*(1-q)+(p-q)^2, four evaluator-only high c4..7 no-op contexts, old A true law H0; keep private evaluation out of learner.
metrics.primary: D_B = old-A Brier at t32 before first return witness on the B-treatment fork minus old-A Brier at t32 on A-continuation fork; two causal worlds are identical up to t16. Same exogenous coins and actions, but observed outcomes can differ as the actual intervention. Paired difference does not isolate learning from changed information.
metrics.secondary: Pre-fork fitted A-slot Brier and digest at t16; per-fork t32 A-slot raw digest/output vs t16, live Brier drift vs t16, phase-belief trajectories, both forks after k=0/1/2/4/8 witnessed return outcomes, frozen old-A readout reference, received/assigned event counts, bytes, elapsed CPU. Explicitly separate protected memory from underlearning.

frozen_hypotheses.P0: Mean fitted A-slot old A high Brier at t16 after the 16 common A witnesses <=0.235, else UNDERTRAINED_BASELINE and no meaningful retention claims.
frozen_hypotheses.H1: Archive mean D_B at t32 <= HMM mean D_B minus .005 and archive D_B lower in >=18 of 24 paired worlds.
frozen_hypotheses.H2: Treatment fork archive return-A high Brier after k4 and k8 witnesses each at least .005 lower than HMM AND archive beats HMM at k8 >=18/24 world pairs.
frozen_hypotheses.H3: Treatment-B fork LIVE old-A slot at t32 must have identical full posterior log-weight bytes, four c4..7 no-op forecasts, and exact cold readout as frozen t16 immediately-after-A snapshot, with ZERO A-slot writes during B; fail when preservation only applies to an immutable reference while the live stored slot changes. Control A fork may continue learning. Both fork t16 snapshots remain cold-restorable.
frozen_hypotheses.H4: Each policy exact cold cloned at t16; 48 sequential one-witness events in both forks per world (16 common prefix duplicated by arm accounting), source-denial and duplicate/order errors, 2304 budget per method across forks, 1920 unique evaluator witness events across 24 worlds, full Ubuntu/Windows regression plus prior real source compatibility.
frozen_hypotheses.classification: Synthetic DEVELOPMENT_SUPPORTED only if P0 and H1 and H2 and H3 and H4; otherwise MIXED/NO_GO. Original SCIENTIFIC_PASS always false; no model promotion.
